input.question: How come games that came out for the 360 in 2005 look really bad compared to some games released in 2013 despite it being on the exact same hardware?
input.ground_truth: The best explanation I have seen is this: One day a dev gets a wooden block with a circle hole in it(console) and he has to take another wooden block(game) and make it fit into that hole. He is getting new tools he isn't sure how to use properly to do this.(New programs and stuff to use for programming and optimising) So for a while the blocks come out butchered and ugly with corners hacked off, but they fit(the game runs but isn't super awesome). 8 years later the devs have learned the tools and made a few new ones and have figured out how to make the block into a perfect circle that fills the hole 100%. In this analogy any gaps between the wooden circle and the hole are wasted power.

Question: How come games that came out for the 360 in 2005 look really bad compared to some games released in 2013 despite it being on the exact same hardware?

Answer:

response.prediction: Okay, let’s imagine the Xbox 360 is like a toy car. Even if all the toy cars are the same model, the ones made later can look and play better because the people making them learned new tricks and got better at building them. So, the games made in 2013 used everything they learned in 8 more years, and made their games look much prettier and work better, even though the toy car (the Xbox 360) didn’t change. It’s like drawing a picture with crayons—when you get older, you can make better drawings with the same crayons!
